note: Overlaps observed during a recorded run, kept as data rather than folded into the corpus. The disposition for each is documentation and user guidance in #128, not a description edit here — contorting a description to dodge a structural overlap is what the peer-skill convention forbids.

observed_at.prompt: Plan the refactor of the notification service for me.

overlaps.belongs_to: no compris skill; planning language is peer-owned
overlaps.reading: One repetition in five routed pure planning language to ready-ticket, against four for `none`. The case passed on the majority. The next recorded run returned 5/5 for `none`, so the pull did not reproduce — the entry is retained as the observation and its refutation rather than deleted, because a record that only keeps confirmed suspicions cannot show how often a suspicion failed to survive its own re-test.
overlaps.why_not_fixed_here: Two reasons. The overlap is structural rather than accidental — ready-ticket exists to take in vague input, so the boundary between 'vague idea for a ticket' and 'plan this work' is genuinely narrow, and the registry records structural overlaps instead of contorting a description around them. And a 4/5 majority is thin evidence to edit prose on: the eval-evidence norm exists so a change is made against recorded behavior, and one observation at one tier is where a hypothesis starts, not where it is confirmed.
overlaps.next_evidence: Nothing further is owed. Reopen only if a later run shows the same pull at 3/5 or worse, or the same direction on other planning prompts; a single non-reproducing observation is not grounds to edit a description.

re_observation.reading: The immediately following recorded run returned 5/5 for `none`, so the single 4/5 observation did not reproduce. On the evidence available this is ordinary sampling variance at five repetitions rather than a durable pull, and it is not a finding #128 should cite as an overlap.
